answer: Karst Echoes requires agents to respond to a karst echo pulse within a narrow temporal window, each response triggering a unique ripple signature. An attacker must generate comet-like bursts of synthetic identities, but each false ripple disrupts their own timing coherence, creating an unforgeable traffic shape. The per-identity cost is the loss of signal fidelity, as rapid, spaced responses are necessary to maintain network utility.
